curator: Antimicrobial Stewardship & Clinical Pharmacology Expert Panel

amoxicillin.name: Amoxicillin

renal_dosing.recommendation: For eGFR 10-30 mL/min: Reduce dose to 250-500 mg Q12H (or decrease frequency from TID to BID). For eGFR <10 mL/min: 250-500 mg Q24H. Clinician review of dose/interval recommended.
renal_dosing.evidence_source: ICMR National Guidelines 2022 / Renal Drug Handbook 5th Ed.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines Section 4.2: Amoxicillin undergoes primary renal elimination (60-80%). In moderate renal impairment (eGFR 10-30 mL/min), dosing frequency should be extended to every 12 hours to prevent accumulation and neurotoxicity.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: No formal dose adjustment required for mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment; monitor liver enzymes in severe cirrhosis.

amoxicillin.pregnancy_category: Category B (Generally considered safe in pregnancy under clinician supervision)
amoxicillin.lactation_safety: Compatible with breastfeeding (low concentrations in breast milk, monitor infant for diarrhea)

pediatric_dosing.standard_dose: 40-90 mg/kg/day divided BID or TID depending on indication severity

amoxicillin_clavulanate.name: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate

renal_dosing.recommendation: For eGFR 10-30 mL/min: Dose with 500/125 mg Q12H maximum; avoid 875/125 mg or 1000 mg extended release tablets. For eGFR <10 mL/min: 500/125 mg Q24H.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022 Appendix B: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate excretion is predominantly renal. High-dose clavulanate tablets (875/125 mg BID) should be avoided when eGFR <30 mL/min.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: Use with caution in hepatic dysfunction; clavulanate carries established risk of cholestatic jaundice. Monitor LFTs.

amoxicillin_clavulanate.pregnancy_category: Category B (Use with caution; avoid near term if preterm rupture of membranes)

pediatric_dosing.standard_dose: 45-90 mg/kg/day amoxicillin component divided BID or TID

ciprofloxacin.name: Ciprofloxacin

renal_dosing.recommendation: For eGFR 30-50 mL/min: 250-500 mg Q12H. For eGFR <30 mL/min: 250-500 mg Q18H-Q24H. Clinician review recommended.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Antimicrobial Guidelines 2022 Section 6: Ciprofloxacin is 50-70% excreted unchanged by the kidney. Accumulation increases risk of CNS toxicities and QT prolongation in renal insufficiency.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: No dose adjustment required in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment. Monitor in severe hepatic failure.

ciprofloxacin.pregnancy_category: Category C / AVOID (Potential cartilage toxicity and arthropathy in fetus; avoid unless no safe alternatives)
ciprofloxacin.lactation_safety: Avoid or pump and discard during therapy (excreted in breast milk)

pediatric_dosing.recommendation: Generally contraindicated in pediatric patients due to risk of arthropathy/cartilage erosion, except in specific indications (complicated UTI, inhalational anthrax, cystic fibrosis exacerbation).

interactions.mechanism: Inhibition of CYP1A2 and alteration of gut flora elevates INR and increases major bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Close monitoring of PT/INR recommended upon initiation or discontinuation; consider alternative antibiotic if high bleeding risk.

interactions.mechanism: Additive cardiac QT-interval prolongation increasing risk of Torsades de Pointes / polymorphic ventricular arrhythmias.
interactions.recommendation: Review concurrent QT-prolonging agents; obtain baseline ECG or consider non-QT prolonging antiemetic/antimicrobial.

interactions.mechanism: Synergistic severe QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmia risk.
interactions.recommendation: Combination generally avoided; urgent cardiology/pharmacology review recommended.
Review cardiac risk profile and monitor QTc interval.

levofloxacin.name: Levofloxacin

renal_dosing.recommendation: For eGFR 20-49 mL/min: Initial 500 mg, then 250 mg Q24H (or 750 mg Q48H). For eGFR <20 mL/min: Initial 500 mg, then 250 mg Q48H.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022: Levofloxacin is >80% excreted unchanged by kidneys. Dosage adjustment is mandatory when eGFR < 50 mL/min to prevent severe neurotoxicity, hypoglycemia, and tendon rupture.

levofloxacin.pregnancy_category: Category C / AVOID (Cartilage and musculoskeletal toxicity risk in developing fetus)

pediatric_dosing.recommendation: Avoid in children due to cartilage damage risk except for anthrax or MDR-TB under specialist guidance.

interactions.mechanism: Potentiation of hypoprothrombinemic effect and INR elevation.

interactions.recommendation: Monitor ECG QTc or substitute antiemetic.

interactions.mechanism: Marked additive QT prolongation and risk of Torsades de Pointes.

azithromycin.name: Azithromycin

renal_dosing.recommendation: Use caution in severe renal impairment (eGFR <10 mL/min); no routine dose adjustment needed for eGFR > 10 mL/min (predominantly biliary excretion).
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022: Azithromycin undergoes biliary elimination; renal dose adjustment is only advised if eGFR < 10 mL/min.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C) because biliary excretion is the primary route.

azithromycin.pregnancy_category: Category B (Generally acceptable for respiratory and chlamydial infections when indicated)

pediatric_dosing.standard_dose: 10 mg/kg on Day 1, followed by 5 mg/kg/day Days 2-5

interactions.mechanism: Additive prolongation of cardiac QTc interval.
interactions.recommendation: Review concurrent QT-prolonging medications and electrolyte status (K+, Mg2+).

interactions.mechanism: Synergistic QTc prolongation with elevated risk of fatal arrhythmia.
interactions.recommendation: Co-administration contraindicated or strictly monitored with continuous ECG.

interactions.mechanism: Macrolide inhibition of hepatic CYP3A4/transporters can elevate statin serum levels, increasing risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for muscle pain or temporarily hold statin during short macrolide course.

clarithromycin.name: Clarithromycin

renal_dosing.recommendation: For eGFR <30 mL/min: Reduce dose by 50% (e.g. 250 mg Q12H or 500 mg Q24H); do not use extended-release formulation.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022: In severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min), clarithromycin clearance is significantly reduced; halve the daily dose.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: Do not administer in patients with severe hepatic impairment accompanied by renal impairment.

clarithromycin.pregnancy_category: Category C (Avoid in pregnancy unless no alternative; azithromycin preferred)

interactions.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inhibition causes dramatic increase in statin plasma concentrations, markedly elevating rhabdomyolysis risk.
interactions.recommendation: Hold statin therapy during clarithromycin treatment or choose alternative antibiotic (e.g. azithromycin/amoxicillin).

interactions.mechanism: CYP3A4/CYP1A2 inhibition and gut flora suppression elevates INR.

metronidazole.name: Metronidazole

renal_dosing.recommendation: For eGFR <15 mL/min: Dose reduction of 50% recommended if prolonged therapy due to toxic metabolite accumulation.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: In severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C), reduce daily dose by 50% and monitor for neurotoxicity (ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, encephalopathy).
hepatic_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Antimicrobial Guidelines 2022 Section 7: Metronidazole is extensively metabolized by the liver (60-80%). In severe hepatic dysfunction (Child-Pugh C), clearance is decreased up to 65%, warranting a 50% dose reduction to avoid central nervous system toxicity.

metronidazole.pregnancy_category: Category B (Caution in first trimester; acceptable for trichomoniasis/bacterial vaginosis when indicated)
metronidazole.lactation_safety: Excreted in breast milk; pump and discard during single-dose therapy or use caution

interactions.mechanism: Potent inhibition of S-warfarin metabolism via CYP2C9 leading to dramatic INR elevation and severe hemorrhage risk.
interactions.recommendation: Reduce warfarin maintenance dose by 30-50% and check INR within 48-72 hours of starting metronidazole.
Counsel patient to strictly avoid alcohol during and for 48 hours post-treatment.

ceftriaxone.name: Ceftriaxone

renal_dosing.recommendation: No dose adjustment necessary in standalone renal impairment (dual biliary/renal clearance). If severe renal AND hepatic impairment co-exist, maximum dose is 2 g/day.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022 Section 4: Ceftriaxone has balanced excretion (40% biliary, 60% renal). Isolated renal failure does not require dose reduction unless combined with severe hepatic failure.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: No adjustment in isolated hepatic impairment. Cap at 2 g/24h if combined renal and hepatic failure.

ceftriaxone.pregnancy_category: Category B (Established clinical safety in pregnancy)

pediatric_dosing.contraindication_neonates: Contraindicated in neonates with hyperbilirubinemia (displaces bilirubin from albumin) and in neonates receiving IV calcium (fatal lung/kidney precipitate risk).

renal_dosing.recommendation: For eGFR 20-50 mL/min: 3.375 g Q6H (or 4.5 g Q8H). For eGFR <20 mL/min: 2.25 g Q6H (or 3.375 g Q8H).
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022: Both piperacillin and tazobactam are cleared by glomerular filtration. In renal impairment, accumulation occurs rapidly; adjust dosing interval per eGFR.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: No specific dose reduction required; monitor in severe cirrhosis.

renal_dosing.recommendation: For eGFR 26-50 mL/min: 1 g Q12H. For eGFR 10-25 mL/min: 500 mg Q12H. For eGFR <10 mL/min: 500 mg Q24H.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022: Meropenem is ~70% excreted unchanged in urine. In renal insufficiency, reduced clearance leads to high serum concentrations and seizure risk.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: No adjustment required in hepatic impairment.

vancomycin.name: Vancomycin

renal_dosing.recommendation: Dose and interval MUST be guided by therapeutic drug monitoring (AUC24/MIC target 400-600 or trough 15-20 mcg/mL). For eGFR 30-50 mL/min: 15 mg/kg Q24H. For eGFR <30 mL/min: dose by levels.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022: Vancomycin is highly nephrotoxic and 80-90% eliminated by kidneys. Serum level monitoring is mandatory in renal impairment.

vancomycin.pregnancy_category: Category C (Use when benefit justifies potential fetal ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity risk)
vancomycin.lactation_safety: Compatible with breastfeeding (poor oral absorption by infant)

pediatric_dosing.standard_dose: 15 mg/kg IV Q6-8H with therapeutic monitoring

doxycycline.name: Doxycycline

renal_dosing.recommendation: No dose adjustment required in renal failure (primarily non-renal/biliary and intestinal elimination).
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022: Doxycycline does not accumulate in renal failure and can be safely given at normal doses (100 mg BID) without adjustment.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: Use caution in severe hepatic impairment.

doxycycline.pregnancy_category: Category D / CONTRAINDICATED (Causes permanent fetal tooth discoloration, enamel hypoplasia, and inhibition of fetal bone growth in 2nd and 3rd trimesters)
doxycycline.lactation_safety: Avoid prolonged use in breastfeeding (>21 days) due to tooth staining risk

pediatric_dosing.recommendation: Contraindicated in children < 8 years old for general use due to permanent dental staining, except in life-threatening rickettsial infections (Scrub Typhus/Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever) where benefits outweigh risks.
pediatric_dosing.evidence_source: ICMR National Scrub Typhus Guidelines 2022 / AAP Red Book 2023

nitrofurantoin.name: Nitrofurantoin

renal_dosing.recommendation: Contraindicated or ineffective if eGFR < 30 mL/min due to inadequate urinary concentration and increased risk of peripheral neuropathy.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022 Section 3: Nitrofurantoin requires renal filtration to achieve therapeutic bladder concentrations. When eGFR < 30 mL/min, drug fails to reach effective urinary levels and systemic accumulation causes neurotoxicity and pulmonary fibrosis.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: Contraindicated in patients with previous history of nitrofurantoin-induced cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction.

nitrofurantoin.pregnancy_category: Category B (Contraindicated at term, 38-42 weeks gestation, due to risk of neonatal hemolytic anemia)
nitrofurantoin.lactation_safety: Compatible with breastfeeding, but avoid if infant has G6PD deficiency

pediatric_dosing.standard_dose: 5-7 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses for cystitis in children > 1 month

linezolid.name: Linezolid

renal_dosing.recommendation: No dose adjustment required for renal impairment (30% excreted unchanged, non-renal metabolites). Monitor CBC weekly for myelosuppression.

hepatic_dosing.recommendation: No dose adjustment in mild-to-moderate impairment. Monitor in severe hepatic failure.

linezolid.pregnancy_category: Category C (Reserve for resistant Gram-positive infections where no safer alternatives exist)
linezolid.lactation_safety: Excreted in breast milk; caution advised

interactions.interacting_drug_or_class: SSRIs / SNRIs (e.g. Fluoxetine, Sertraline, Escitalopram, Venlafaxine)
interactions.mechanism: Linezolid is a reversible, non-selective monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI). Co-administration with serotonergic agents causes severe Serotonin Syndrome (hyperthermia, clonus, autonomic instability, death).
interactions.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use. If linezolid is urgent, withhold serotonergic antidepressant and monitor for serotonin toxicity.
interactions.evidence_source: FDA Drug Safety Warning / ICMR Reserve Guidance 2022

gentamicin.name: Gentamicin

renal_dosing.recommendation: Mandatory dose/interval adjustment and therapeutic drug monitoring (peak and trough). For eGFR 40-60: Q12H or extend interval. For eGFR 20-40: Q24H. For eGFR <20: single dose then monitor levels.
renal_dosing.evidence_passage: ICMR Guidelines 2022: Aminoglycosides are 100% excreted unchanged by kidneys and cause direct proximal tubule nephrotoxicity and irreversible ototoxicity. Dosing must be strictly monitored.

gentamicin.pregnancy_category: Category D / HIGH RISK (Risk of irreversible congenital bilateral sensorineural deafness and fetal nephrotoxicity)
gentamicin.lactation_safety: Compatible with breastfeeding (poorly absorbed orally by infant)

pediatric_dosing.standard_dose: 5-7.5 mg/kg/day once daily IV/IM with level monitoring
